title: Anthropic upgrades Claude Code Projects to run parallel AI workers
lede: Anthropic has rebuilt Projects in Claude Code so a coordinator splits a goal into parallel threads, each a cloud session on its own branch, then reviews and assembles the results.

points: Each thread is a full Claude Code cloud session with its own branch and repo copy; overlapping edits surface as ordinary merge conflicts.
Threads share a project memory and a library of files and artifacts, so context builds up as work continues.
Users steer from the main project chat or inside a single thread, including from a phone, and work carries on while they are away.
The beta starts with some Pro and Max subscribers on cloud sessions; Team and Enterprise plans come later.
Anthropic warns projects can hit usage limits faster and lets users set model and effort for the coordinator and workers; local threads are coming.

points.text: A team member says the coordinator formalises the habit of running many agents in parallel; a reply says sub-agents burned a whole usage allowance in ten minutes.
Cost is the recurring worry, with commenters expecting parallel threads to multiply API spend.
Others object that it runs only in Anthropic's cloud, pulling the execution environment under one vendor's control.
Some say homegrown setups already do this, from CalDAV to-do queues picked up by an LLM to GitHub issues plus worktrees.
